title: Pasting of normalized strict-tower inverse-image squares
statement: Let B be any commutative ring, and use the strict-tower derived inverse-image functors G and section-normalized compositors gComp of [def-cbc-strict-constant-tower-operations], and squareG of [def-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-arrows]. For scheme maps j:U→X, j₁:U₁→X₁, j₂:U₂→X₂, g:X₁→X, h:X₂→X₁, a:U₁→U, b:U₂→U₁ with a≫j=j₁≫g and b≫j₁=j₂≫h, let w be the induced equality (b≫a)≫j=j₂≫(h≫g). For any N∈D(Towers(B,X)), gComp(b,a) at G_j N followed by G_b of squareG(a,j₁,j,g) inverse at N and squareG(b,j₂,j₁,h) inverse at G_g N equals squareG(b≫a,j₂,j,h≫g) inverse at N followed by G_j₂ of gComp(h,g) at N. All maps are the specified canonical comparisons; no openness or cartesianness is assumed.

proof.text: Expand each concrete squareG as the inverse equality-indexed compositor followed by the other compositor. The private squareG_eq proves this directly from normalizeIsoSquare, avoiding specialization of a generic category-family law. Replace gComp by gCompEq at reflexive equations using gCompEq_refl. Evaluate the already proved concrete gCompEq_coherence at N for the triples (b,a,j), (b,j₁,g), and (j₂,h,g). Rearrange the first two equations with rearrange_square, rewrite the first two successive factors, and cancel the adjacent inverse compositor. The last associativity equation gives the outer square followed by the bottom compositor. All calculations retain the original explicit component statement and its canonical derived-category instances. No openness or cartesianness is used.

theorem squareG_pasting_inv {U U₁ U₂ X X₁ X₂ : Scheme.{u}}
    (j : U ⟶ X) (j₁ : U₁ ⟶ X₁) (j₂ : U₂ ⟶ X₂)
    (g : X₁ ⟶ X) (h : X₂ ⟶ X₁) (a : U₁ ⟶ U) (b : U₂ ⟶ U₁)
    (w₁ : a ≫ j = j₁ ≫ g) (w₂ : b ≫ j₁ = j₂ ≫ h)
    (w : (b ≫ a) ≫ j = j₂ ≫ (h ≫ g)) (N : Derived B X) :
    (gComp B b a).hom.app ((G B j).obj N) ≫
        (G B b).map ((squareG B a j₁ j g w₁).inv.app N) ≫
        (squareG B b j₂ j₁ h w₂).inv.app ((G B g).obj N) =
      (squareG B (b ≫ a) j₂ j (h ≫ g) w).inv.app N ≫
        (G B j₂).map ((gComp B h g).hom.app N)
